scope: Scalar translational or rotational elastic connectors between existing explicit native Rigid Body ports, or one port to ground; small-displacement linear static 3D solid analyses only.
coupling: Users create Fem::ConstraintRigidBody objects and explicitly select persistent CAD regions. No hidden rigidification, inferred region, node-wise stiffness division, equivalent lever or default engineering stiffness is introduced. ReferenceNode remains the existing native body's explicitly entered global position, not a new associative anchor.
mechanism: Stock CalculiX RIGID BODY with distinct reference and rotation nodes. Rotational nodes do not belong to elements: an EQUATION projects their three global rotation components to a scalar auxiliary DOF1 connected by SPRING1/2. Auxiliary DOFs2/3 are computational zeros, not physical body restraints. Translational ports use the reference node and existing spring orientation.
outputs: Raw global node U/RF are requested. RF is not generally an isolated connector-action result in a connected assembly. Signed actions are qualified on separately constrained exact benchmark models.
identity: Native body links, CAD region links, occurrence placements and orientation references persist. Region nodes are resolved against the current mesh, never cached by old node ID; sparse mesh IDs are allocated safely and native save/reopen mesh compaction is permitted. Changed occurrences with an old mesh fail closed.
reference_sections: CalculiX 2.23 manual: RIGID BODY pp589-590 and SPRING pp598-599; prior verified manual provenance in freecad-ctq-contract.json.
engineering_limit: Capability qualification does not supply project Kser, justify rigid coupling for a particular connection, or accept any building design.
